look_here_first: First inspect alternate leaves (often coarsely toothed but occasionally entire) and narrow cylindrical flower heads. Use a loupe to check 18–22 phyllaries in 5–6 overlapping series and 13–20 disk florets. At fruiting, confirm mostly hairless cypselae with 30–35 tawny pappus bristles. Do not use river-gravel habitat or leaf teeth alone.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Kew accepts Texas native species, but exact three-county project threshold was not reviewed in this installation; native-only metrics excluded pending independent range review.

morphology_keys.habit: Branched woody shrub about 60–120 cm; stems finely hairy and sparsely gland-dotted.
morphology_keys.leaves: Alternate, short-petiolate (1–2 mm); blades lanceolate to lance-ovate, 5–40 × 3.5–12 mm, faintly three-veined from base; margins usually coarsely toothed but sometimes entire; gland dots.
morphology_keys.heads: Narrow panicle of cylindrical to bell-shaped involucres 7–11 mm, phyllaries 18–22 in 5–6 series, florets 13–20, pale green/yellow tubular disk corollas.
morphology_keys.fruits: Cypselae 3.5–4 mm, usually glabrous; 30–35 tawny barbellate to subplumose pappus bristles.
best_field_traits: Mostly hairless mature cypselae with tawny bristles

comparisons.key_distinctions: B. dentata typically has alternate, toothed leaves and mostly glabrous cypselae; B. cylindracea frequently has opposite/subopposite leaves with a woolly underside; B. eupatorioides usually has opposite leaves and often subplumose pappus. Confirm with mature heads and fruits, not leaf position alone.
comparisons.cautions: Leaf teeth and leaf arrangement vary; compare several mature nodes and mature cypselae. Do not force a separation on sterile material.
